name: Ryzen 5 5500
note: Cheapest current chip that never bottlenecks an entry GPU at 1080p.

name: Ryzen 5 5600
note: The value AM4 gaming pick if you already own DDR4.

name: Ryzen 7 5700X3D
note: 3D cache on AM4 — a large lift for an ageing platform without a new board.

name: Ryzen 5 8600G
note: APU for a no-GPU starter build; add a discrete card later.

name: Ryzen 5 7600
note: AM5 entry point — socket support runs years past this build.

name: Ryzen 5 9600X
note: Zen 5 six-core; a little faster and cooler than the 7600.

name: Ryzen 5 7600X3D
note: Cheapest way into 3D V-Cache gaming on AM5.

name: Ryzen 7 7700
note: Eight cores hold 1% lows in open-world titles without pushing the budget.

name: Ryzen 7 9700X
note: Zen 5 eight-core; strong all-rounder short of the X3D.

name: Ryzen 7 7800X3D
note: The 1440p/4K gaming default — cache beats clocks in most engines.

name: Ryzen 9 7900X
note: Twelve cores for mixed gaming and content work.

name: Ryzen 9 9900X
note: Zen 5 twelve-core, far cooler and quieter than the 7900X.

name: Ryzen 7 9800X3D
note: Fastest gaming CPU we track; zero CPU bottleneck at any resolution.

name: Ryzen 9 9950X3D
note: 3D cache plus sixteen cores — top-tier gaming and heavy multi-thread.

name: Core i5-14600KF
note: Last-gen LGA1700 value; cheap boards and a DDR4 option.

name: Core Ultra 5 245K
note: Arrow Lake mid-tier; efficient, strong in productivity, average in games.

name: Core Ultra 7 265K
note: Twenty cores; matches the 9900X outside gaming, trails it inside.

name: Core Ultra 9 285K
note: Intel flagship; a content-creation chip more than a gaming one.

name: GeForce RTX 5050
note: Entry RT card for esports and older titles at 1080p.

name: Radeon RX 7600
note: Best cost-per-frame at 1080p high in our benchmark set.

name: Arc B580
note: 12GB at the entry price; drivers are mature now.

name: GeForce RTX 5060
note: 1080p with DLSS 4 and usable ray tracing; 8GB is the limit.

name: Radeon RX 9060 8GB
note: 1080p Radeon option; step to the XT for the 16GB buffer.

name: GeForce RTX 5060 Ti 8GB
note: Clears 100 FPS at 1080p ultra across our whole title set.

name: Radeon RX 9060 XT 16GB
note: Twice the VRAM of the 8GB NVIDIA cards near this price.

name: Arc B770
note: Intel's step-up card; strong in modern low-level APIs.

name: GeForce RTX 5060 Ti 16GB
note: The 16GB buffer is the one to buy at this tier for 1440p longevity.

name: Radeon RX 7700 XT
note: Last-gen 1440p card, frequently discounted below the 9060 XT.

name: GeForce RTX 5070
note: Median 112 FPS at 1440p ultra across our benchmark set.

name: Radeon RX 9070
note: Raster-comparable to the 5070 with 16GB; weaker ray tracing.

name: Radeon RX 9070 XT
note: Matches the 5070 Ti in raster for less; FSR instead of DLSS 4.

name: GeForce RTX 5070 Ti
note: 16GB frame buffer keeps 1440p ultra and 4K upscaled both in range.

name: GeForce RTX 5080
note: Sustains 4K high-refresh with ray tracing enabled in our set.

name: Radeon RX 9080 XT
note: Radeon's halo raster card; 24GB for local AI work as well as 4K.

name: GeForce RTX 5090
note: No-compromise 4K; needs a 1000 W-class ATX 3.1 supply.

name: B550M PRO-VDH
note: Cheapest board on our QVL with a proper VRM for a Ryzen 5.

name: B550 Tomahawk
note: The AM4 board to keep; overbuilt power for anything up to a 5800X3D.

name: B650M Pro RS
note: Wi-Fi onboard and DDR5-6000 on the QVL without paying for X670.

name: B650 Tomahawk Wi-Fi
note: Overbuilt VRM and 4× M.2 — the upgrade-friendly AM5 pick.

name: TUF B650-E Wi-Fi
note: PCIe 5.0 graphics slot for the next GPU generation.

name: ROG Strix B650E-I
note: The ITX AM5 board that does not compromise on VRM or M.2 count.

name: ROG Crosshair X670E Hero
note: Everything AM5 offers, plus the layout for open-loop cooling.

name: ROG Strix X870E-E
note: Full PCIe 5.0 lanes, Wi-Fi 7 and four Gen5 M.2 slots.

name: PRO B760M-A DDR4
note: Lets a 14600KF reuse an existing DDR4 kit to save on the build.

name: B860 Tomahawk Wi-Fi
note: The sensible Arrow Lake board; skip Z890 unless you overclock memory hard.

name: MPG Z890 Carbon Wi-Fi
note: Z890 for high memory clocks and full Gen5 storage on Intel.

name: ROG Strix B860-I
note: Small-form Intel option with a heatsink that can take a 265K.

name: 16GB DDR4-3200 CL16
note: Dual-channel 16GB is the floor for modern titles; 3200 is free performance.

name: 32GB DDR4-3600 CL16
note: The last DDR4 kit worth buying — 3600 CL16 for Ryzen 5000 or LGA1700.

name: 32GB DDR5-5600 CL46
note: JEDEC-spec DDR5; fine for Intel, leaves EXPO tuning to the enthusiast kits.

name: 32GB DDR5-6000 CL30
note: The Ryzen sweet spot — matched to the memory controller's 1:1 ceiling.

name: 32GB DDR5-6000 CL28
note: CL28 kit binned for X3D chips; measurable in CPU-bound scenes.

name: 32GB DDR5-6400 CL30
note: A-die kit for boards that hold 6400 at 1:1 on the current revision.

name: 64GB DDR5-6000 CL30
note: Two-DIMM 64GB — the right way to get there without losing memory clock.

name: 64GB DDR5-6400 CL32
note: 64GB for large project files or many VMs alongside the game.

name: 96GB DDR5-6000 CL34
note: Non-binary 48GB DIMMs — maximum capacity that still runs dual-rank fast.

name: P3 1TB NVMe
note: Fast enough for game loads at the lowest cost per TB we track.

name: P3 Plus 2TB NVMe
note: Doubles capacity and adds Gen4 speed; still the cheapest per-TB drive we track.

name: SN770 1TB NVMe
note: Gen4 speeds for near-Gen3 money; DirectStorage ready.

name: SN770 2TB NVMe
note: Same controller as the 1TB, double the capacity, no speed penalty.

name: 990 EVO 2TB NVMe
note: 2TB is the practical floor once three or four modern titles are installed.

name: 990 PRO 2TB NVMe
note: Full-DRAM drive — sustained writes hold up under back-to-back game installs.

name: 990 PRO 4TB NVMe
note: 4TB of DRAM-cached Gen4 — never think about install management again.

name: T500 2TB NVMe
note: 990 PRO performance, usually a little cheaper, runs cooler under load.

name: T705 2TB NVMe
note: Gen5 speed; only worth it with a heatsink and a real DirectStorage workload.

name: T705 4TB NVMe
note: Gen5 capacity drive — no install management, no second SSD.

name: BarraCuda 4TB HDD
note: Cold-storage spinner for recordings and libraries you rarely load.

name: CX550 550W Bronze
note: 160 W of headroom over an entry build's measured peak draw.

name: MAG A650BN 650W Gold
note: 650 W covers transient GPU spikes on a 60-class card with 40% margin.

name: RM750e 750W Gold
note: Native 12V-2×6 connector and ATX 3.1 transient compliance for 70-class cards.

name: RM850x 850W Gold

name: RM1000x 1000W Gold
note: 1000 W for an 80-class card with headroom for the generation after.

name: Vertex GX-1000 1000W
note: Seasonic platform, tight regulation, 12-year warranty.

name: PRIME TX-1300 1300W Titanium
note: Titanium efficiency and a fan that stays off below ~40% load — for a 5090.

name: SF750 750W Platinum
note: SFX unit for ITX cases; 750 W is enough for everything up to a 5070 Ti.

name: FOCUS GX-650 650W Gold
note: Alternative 650 W Gold unit with a longer warranty than the MSI.

name: GX III Gold 850
note: Cheaper 850 W ATX 3.1 option when the RM850x is out of stock.
